sections.title: Sargability — Write Predicates That Use Indexes

blocks.md: **SARGable = Search ARGument ABLE. Predicate can use index seek. Non-sargable → Seq Scan. Rule: column naked on one side, constant on other. No functions, no math, no implicit casts on column.**

blocks.label: sargable vs non-sargable
blocks.code:
-- SARGABLE (index seek)
WHERE created_at >= '2024-01-01'
WHERE name LIKE 'Alice%'
WHERE dept_id IN (1,2,3)
WHERE salary > 50000

-- NON-SARGABLE (Seq Scan)
WHERE UPPER(name) = 'ALICE'           -- function on column
WHERE created_at + INTERVAL '1 day' > NOW()  -- math on column
WHERE YEAR(created_at) = 2024         -- function
WHERE salary * 1.1 > 55000            -- math
WHERE name LIKE '%smith'              -- leading wildcard
WHERE status = 'active' OR status = 'pending'  -- OR often kills index
blocks.pg:
-- Partial index makes OR sargable for known values
CREATE INDEX idx_status_active ON employees (id) WHERE status IN ('active','pending');
blocks.mysql:
-- Functional index (MySQL 8.0+)
CREATE INDEX idx_email_lower ON users ((LOWER(email)));
blocks.py-pandas:
# No index concept, but vectorized ops:
# Good: df[df['created_at'] >= '2024-01-01']
# Bad: df[df['created_at'].dt.year == 2024]  # computes year for all rows

blocks.md: **Implicit cast kills index too.** `WHERE varchar_col = 123` casts column to numeric → Seq Scan. `WHERE numeric_col = '123'` is fine (constant cast). Always match types.

options: Function/math on column prevents index use
items.explain: Any computation on column (math, function, cast) prevents B-tree traversal.

revisionCard: SARGable: column naked on left, constant on right. No functions/math/casts on column
Functional index: index the expression (LOWER, math) to make non-sargable sargable
Partial index: WHERE clause on index — smaller, faster for skewed access patterns
Predicate pushdown: move filter to storage layer; key in distributed/columnar DBs
Covering index (INCLUDE): index-only scan, avoids heap fetch
Implicit cast on column = Seq Cast. Match types: numeric_col = 123 not '123'

glossary.def: Search ARGument ABLE — predicate that can use index seek (e.g., col = 5).
Index on expression (e.g., LOWER(col)) — supports queries using that expression.
Index with WHERE clause — only indexes subset of rows matching condition.
Index with INCLUDE columns — satisfies query without heap lookup.
Moving filter predicate down to storage/index layer to reduce data movement.
Automatic type conversion on column (e.g., varchar = 123) — kills index.
